cards.text: Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite is a young man who waited to speak because the others were older. Now Job's three friends have no further reply. So Elihu turns to Job and says, "But now, O Job, hear my speech, and listen to all my words."
Elihu says, "Behold, I will open my mouth; my address is on the tip of my tongue." This man has been sitting on this speech like a coworker with his hand up for the WHOLE meeting.

cards.question: Elihu wants Job to trust what he's about to say. Where does Elihu say his words come from?

cards.text: Then Elihu says, "The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life." That's a BIG opener, friend, because when I start a speech, I open with "Uh, is this thing on?"

cards.question: Elihu isn't asking Job to just nod along. What does he invite Job to do?

cards.text: Then Elihu says, "I am just like you before God; I was also formed from clay." Translation: same batch, friend, and nobody here is the fancy cookie.

cards.question: Since they're both formed from clay, Elihu tells Job that Job should be terrified of him.

cards.text: Now Elihu gets specific. He tells Job he heard him say, "I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, with no iniquity in me."

cards.question: Elihu keeps quoting Job's complaint. Job said God finds occasions against him: "He counts me as His ___."

cards.text: Elihu quotes Job one more time: "He puts my feet in the stocks; He watches over all my paths." He's reading Job's own words back to him, like a coworker who saved your email and brought it to the meeting.

cards.question: After quoting Job's words, Elihu tells Job that he is right in this matter.
Elihu tells Job he's not right in this matter, and says he'll answer him. What reason does Elihu give?
Elihu asks Job, "Why do you complain to Him that He answers ___ a man asks?"

cards.text: Now Elihu answers that complaint: "For God speaks in one way and in another, yet no one notices." Like a phone buzzing on silent all day, and we're the ones not checking it.

cards.question: Elihu describes one of the ways God speaks. When deep sleep falls on people as they slumber on their beds, how does God speak?

answers.text: In a dream or a vision

cards.text: In the night, He opens their ears and terrifies them with warnings. We've all had a dream that sat us straight up in bed, friend, but THIS is a whole other level.

cards.question: Why does God send those warnings? Elihu says it's "to turn a man from wrongdoing and keep him from ___"
Those night warnings protect a man from something big. What does Elihu say they preserve his soul from?

cards.text: Then Elihu says a man is also chastened on his bed. He's there with pain and constant distress in his bones.

cards.question: Elihu says the man lying in pain still enjoys his favorite food.

cards.text: His flesh wastes away, and his hidden bones protrude. He draws near to the Pit, and his life to the messengers of death.
But what if there's a messenger on his side, one mediator in a thousand, to tell him what is right for him? One in a THOUSAND, friend, like the coworker who actually stays late to help you finish.

cards.question: That messenger is gracious to the man and says to spare him from going down to the Pit. What does the messenger say he has found?
Once the man is spared, Elihu says his flesh is refreshed like a child's, and he returns to the days of his youth.

cards.text: He prays to God and finds favor, he sees God's face and shouts for joy, and God restores His righteousness to that man. Worn out to brand new, friend, and after my years in that junk drawer, I KNOW that feeling.

cards.question: Then the restored man sings before men. What does his song admit?

answers.text: He sinned but didn't get what he deserved
He was innocent the whole time

cards.question: In his song, the restored man takes the credit for saving himself from the Pit.

cards.text: Elihu sums it up: God does all these things to a man, two or even three times. Friend, it took me more than three tries just to learn which side of the stamp goes down.

cards.question: Why does Elihu say God does all these things to a man?

answers.text: To bring back his soul from the Pit
To test how much he can take
To win an argument with him

cards.text: Then Elihu turns back to Job: "Pay attention, Job, and listen to me; be silent, and I will speak." That's the second time in this speech he's asked Job to listen, and I respect a man who knows what he wants.

cards.question: But Elihu leaves the door open. If Job has something to say, Elihu tells him to speak up, "for I would like to ___ you."

cards.text: And if Job has nothing to say, Elihu tells him to be quiet, and he'll teach him wisdom. Stick around, friend, because this teaching isn't done yet.

findings.problem: The card names Elihu as 'son of Barachel the Buzite', which comes from Job 32:2. The citation starts at Job 32:4, so it leaves out a verse the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: In 'Elihu tells Job that he is right in this matter,' the word 'he' can mean Elihu or Job. Elihu does claim he is right, since he says he will answer Job because God is greater than man. A baker could argue True.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The card opens with 'In the night,' which comes from Job 33:15. The card cites only Job 33:16.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'He sinned but didn't get what he deserved,' is noticeably longer than the wrong answers ('He was innocent the whole time', 'He earned his healing himself'). Its two-part 'but' shape also makes it stand out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: In Job 33:29, the core action is God repeating His rescue two or three times. The joke is about Papa Dorin failing and needing many tries to learn something. That is a different action: a slow learner, not a persistent rescuer. The image of a stamper learning 'which side of the stamp goes down' also doesn't click right away.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: From card 5 to card 16, the question types alternate in a fixed pattern: multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice. Both stops also end on a fill in the blank.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
